title: pvAngularPeriodicFilter
body:
## pvAngularPeriodicFilter

Rebuilds a full rotor or periodic set of sectors from a computed sector: selected blocks are copied and rotated about an axis (X, Y or Z through Center) by multiples of an angle, rotating point coordinates and 3- and 9-component arrays (vectors and tensors) consistently. Each selected leaf becomes a multipiece of rotated copies, the first being the original; with IterationMode Maximum (ParaView default) there are round(360 / angle) copies, otherwise NumberOfPeriods. The angle is RotationAngle in degrees (default 10) or read in radians from a field array. VTK supports polydata, structured and unstructured grid leaves.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- For multiblock input only blocks listed in BlockIndices are rotated; with none listed the output is an unchanged copy. A single non-composite dataset is always processed.
- Rotated arrays are computed on the fly by default (ComputeRotationsOnTheFly), saving memory but costing time at every access.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `AngularPeriodicFilter`. Identity: `filters/AngularPeriodicFilter`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Periodic filter. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Axis` | This property specifies the axis of rotation | `{"type":"enum","values":["Axis X","Axis Y","Axis Z"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Axis X"` |
| `BlockIndices` | This property lists the ids of the blocks to make periodic from the input multiblock dataset. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1]` |
| `Center` | This property specifies the 3D coordinates for the center of the rotation. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `ComputeRotationsOnTheFly` | Specify whether the rotations should be computed on-the-fly, which is compute intensive, or if the arrays should be explicitly generated and stored, at the cost of using more memory. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `IterationMode` | This property specifies the mode of iteration, either a user-provided number of periods, or the maximum number of periods to rotate to 360 degrees. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Manual","Maximum"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Manual"` |
| `NumberOfPeriods` | This property specifies the number of iteration | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `RotationAngle` | Rotation angle in degree. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `RotationArrayName` | Field array name that contains the rotation angle in radians. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `RotationMode` | This property specifies the mode of rotation, either from a user provided angle or from an array in the data. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Direct Angle","Array Value"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Direct Angle"` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvAngularPeriodicFilter",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
